This is designed from the beginning considering OpenTelemetry's contrib current implementation, Logfire, and Sentry.

title: 🐛 Fix deadlock that can occur when closing dependencies during response model validation
body:
Related to #5122

In my project, I had noticed I was getting a sqlalchemy `QueuePool` limit error like others had noted in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/6628. This was marked as probably fixed by https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/5122.

Even on fastapi commit `e4727ed2` (> v0.112.2), you can still run into this issue when running the tests created by the author of #5122 - https://github.com/harsh8398/fastapi-dependency-issue. I also notice others running into similar deadlocks after picking up the `0.82.0` patch: https://github.com/vipyrsec/dragonfly-mainframe/issues/235.

The author of the issue/discussion #6628 noted that when adding a `response_model` to the endpoint function, they noticed that the suggested quick fixes (i.e. using a contextmanager, async session manager, etc.) didn't seem to work either. It seems like the response model validation runs into the same issue that when using `Depends`, a deadlock can occur when closing sessions.

I believe this pr fixes this `Depends` issue all the way.

I tested this pr against https://github.com/harsh8398/fastapi-dependency-issue and notice that all test cases pass equally as fast! This patch also fixes the deadlocks/timeouts I was seeing in my own codebase.

**UPD YuriiMotov:** related discussion on SQLModel repo (https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/discussions/1417)

body:
Bumps [anyio](https://github.com/agronholm/anyio) from 4.12.1 to 4.14.2.
Release notes

Sourced from anyio's releases.

4.14.2

  • Changed ByteReceiveStream.receive() implementations to raise a ValueError when max_bytes is not a positive integer (#1191)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting float("inf") when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop. The adapter setter checked for infinity by identity (value is math.inf), so only the exact math.inf singleton was accepted, while every backend setter (using math.isinf()) accepts any positive infinity (#1189; PR by @​greymoth-jp).
  • Fixed to_process.run_sync() deadlocking when the worker function writes enough data to sys.stderr to fill the (undrained) pipe buffer. The worker process now redirects sys.stderr to os.devnull as well, matching the documented behavior
  • Fixed TLSStream.wrap() matching an internationalized (unicode) host name against the peer certificate using IDNA 2003 (via the standard library) instead of IDNA 2008, which could cause the host name to be matched against the wrong certificate (#1208)
  • Fixed anyio.open_process() (and run_process()) ignoring the extra_groups argument, as it mistakenly passed the value of the group argument instead (#1209)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait() and CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait_on_behalf_of() raising trio.WouldBlock instead of anyio.WouldBlock on the trio backend when there are no tokens available (#1218)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter on the asyncio backend over-granting tokens (borrowed_tokens exceeding total_tokens and available_tokens going negative) when a non-blocking acquire was made in the window between a token being released and the notified waiter resuming. The freed token is now reserved for the woken waiter right away, so the non-blocking acquire correctly raises WouldBlock (#1170; PR by @​gaoflow)
  • Fixed unnecessary CPU spin when delivering cancellation from CancelScope on asyncio under certain conditions, including improper cancel scope nesting (#1111)

4.14.1

  • Fixed teardown of higher-scoped async fixtures failing on asyncio with RuntimeError: Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task than it was entered in when an async test raise an outcome exception (e.g., pytest.skip(), pytest.xfail(), or pytest.fail()) (#1179; PR by @​EmmanuelNiyonshuti)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting a value of 0 when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop, contradicting the documented behavior of allowing 0 total tokens (#1183; PR by @​nyxst4ck)

4.14.0

title: Use an explicit response_model as the item type on streaming endpoints
body:
Discussed in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16382.

On a streaming (generator) endpoint, `response_model` is only turned into a per-item field when it is left to the return annotation. Passing it explicitly silently disables both validation and the `response_model_*` options, and leaves the OpenAPI `itemSchema` empty:

```python
class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    secret: str

@app.get("/stream", response_model=Item, response_model_exclude={"secret"})
def stream():
    yield Item(name="public", secret="private")
```

Before this change the endpoint streams `{"name": "public", "secret": "private"}`, so a field the developer asked to exclude is served to the client, and the OpenAPI response is `{"application/jsonl": {"itemSchema": {}}}`. Writing `response_model=Iterable[Item]` instead does not help: it is rejected outright as an invalid response field.

`_populate_api_route_state` resolves the stream item type only inside the `isinstance(response_model, DefaultPlaceholder)` branch. With an explicit model, `route.stream_item_type` stays `None`, `stream_item_field` is never built, and `_serialize_data` falls back to `jsonable_encoder` plus `json.dumps`, which is the path that skips validation and the exclusion options.

An explicit `response_model` on a streaming endpoint now feeds `stream_item_field` the same way the return annotation does, and both the item type and an iterable of it are accepted. Afterwards the endpoint above streams `{"name": "public"}` and its OpenAPI response carries `itemSchema: {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Item"}`.

The new branch only applies to generator endpoints whose response class is the default placeholder (JSONL) or `EventSourceResponse` (SSE), and it keeps the existing `ServerSentEvent` exclusion, since that is a transport wrapper rather than a data model. Non-streaming endpoints, bare iterables and return-annotation streams are untouched.

## Tests

`tests/test_stream_explicit_response_model.py` covers sync and async generators, `Iterable[Item]` and `AsyncIterable[Item]`, `response_model_exclude` and `response_model_exclude_none`, SSE, per-item validation, and the OpenAPI schema, together with a non-streaming endpoint to pin that its behaviour is unchanged. On `master` the module fails at import, because `response_model=Iterable[Item]` raises `FastAPIError`.

The rest of the suite passes: 2046 passed, 12 skipped (`tests/`, excluding `benchmarks` and `test_tutorial`, which need optional extras not installed here).

title: 🐛 Prevent stale endpoint context cache entries
body:
## Problem

`_extract_endpoint_context()` caches endpoint metadata by `id(func)` without retaining or validating the function object. After an endpoint is collected, Python can reuse that id for another endpoint, causing validation errors and logs to report the wrong file, line, or function.

## Solution

Store a weak reference alongside each cached context and validate the referenced object with `is` before using a cache hit. Callable objects that do not support weak references are still handled correctly and are recomputed instead of being retained.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest -q tests/test_endpoint_context_cache.py tests/test_custom_route_class.py tests/test_custom_middleware_exception.py tests/test_callable_endpoint.py` (10 passed)
- `uv run mypy fastapi/routing.py` (passed)
- `uv run ty check fastapi/routing.py` (passed)
- `uv run bash scripts/test.sh` (3,347 passed, 18 skipped, 5 xfailed locally; the optional CLI test was unavailable because `fastapi[standard]` was not installed)
- Fork preflight run [35815878739](https://github.com/rksharma-owg/fastapi/actions/runs/35815878739) passed the full test script on Ubuntu 3.13, macOS 3.10, and Windows 3.12 for commit `914469e4cefd8085abd3020c470a8c2e022bdd16`.

Fixes #16390

title: 👷 Fix coverage badge: keep Smokeshow HTML under size limit and fail on upload errors
body:
The coverage badge in the README currently shows `coverage ??%`. The badge worker reports:

```
No status found which matched regex ^coverage, status descriptions: []
```

No `smokeshow / coverage` status has been posted on `master` since #14992 (2026-02-27). The last commits before it (e.g. 4fce9ce, 728b097) have `Coverage 100.00%`; every code commit after it has none.

## Root cause

#14992 replaced coverage's `dynamic_context = "test_function"` with pytest-cov's `--cov-context=test`. pytest-cov records one context per parametrized case **and** per phase (`|setup`, `|run`, `|teardown`), e.g.:

```
Linux-py3.13-no-deprecation|tests/test_request_params/test_cookie/test_optional_str.py::test_optional_alias_by_alias[/optional-alias]|run
```

The combined data now has ~20k contexts, and with `show_contexts = true` the generated `htmlcov` grew to **~68 MB**, over Smokeshow's 50 MB site limit. Every upload fails with:

```
ERROR! ... status=429 response=429: You've exceeded the site size limit of 52428800.
```

Since the status is only posted after a successful upload, it's never set.

This went unnoticed because the retry loop in `smokeshow.yml` ends with `sleep 1` when all 5 attempts fail, so the step exits 0 and the Smokeshow workflow is green.

## Changes

* `test.yml`: generate the HTML report with `--omit "tests/*"`. This keeps the per-test contexts for `fastapi/` and `docs_src/` (the useful part, "which test covers this line"), while dropping the per-file pages for the test files themselves. `coverage report --fail-under=100` is unchanged and still checks tests.
* `smokeshow.yml`: exit with an error if all upload attempts fail, so this kind of breakage is visible.

## Verification

Using the coverage artifacts from the latest `master` Test run (50113da):

| | HTML size | total |
|---|---|---|
| current | 68 MB | 100% |
| with `--omit "tests/*"` | 35 MB | 100% |

(For reference, disabling `show_contexts` entirely gives 41 MB; this approach keeps contexts and leaves more headroom.)

Also checked the upload loop with a stubbed command: exits `1` when every attempt fails, `0` on success.

title: 🐛 Fix endpoint context shared and mutated across requests
body:
_extract_endpoint_context() caches the context dict per endpoint function and returned the cached dict itself. The request handler (and the WebSocket handler) then set endpoint_ctx["path"] on it, mutating the shared cached object.

When the same endpoint function is used by more than one route (or the same route handles concurrent requests), the path stored in a RequestValidationError / ResponseValidationError could be overwritten by another request, so error messages and logs reported the wrong route.

Return a copy of the cached context so each request gets its own dict.

title: fix: serialize WebSocket validation errors to JSON string in close reason
body:
The default `websocket_request_validation_exception_handler` currently passes the result of `jsonable_encoder(exc.errors())` directly to `WebSocket.close()` as the `reason`.

`jsonable_encoder(exc.errors())` returns a list, while `WebSocket.close()` expects `reason` to be a `str | None`. As a result, WebSocket request-validation errors can cause the exception handler itself to fail instead of closing the connection with the intended `1008` policy-violation code.

This change serializes the validation errors with `json.dumps()` before passing them to `WebSocket.close()`. The reason is therefore a valid string containing machine-readable JSON.

A regression test was added to verify that:

- WebSocket request-validation failures close with code `1008`.
- The close reason is a string.
- The reason contains the expected validation error.
- The behavior fails with the previous implementation and passes with this fix.

The change is intentionally minimal and does not alter the validation behavior or the WebSocket close code.

body:
When a path operation returns content with a status code that must not have a body (e.g. 205 set via status_code or the Response parameter), FastAPI empties response.body, but the Content-Length header was already computed by the response class from the original content. Reset the Content-Length header to 0 when the body is dropped.

title: 📝 Document custom headers for JSONL and SSE streams
body:
## Pull Request

Discussion: N/A - docs-only clarification with tutorial test coverage.

## Description

This PR documents how to add custom response headers to JSON Lines and SSE streaming endpoints.

FastAPI already documents the common pattern in [Response Headers](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/response-headers/): use a `Response` parameter and mutate `response.headers`. This PR adds the streaming-specific caveat. For generator endpoints, setting a header inside the generator body is too late because FastAPI has already prepared the streaming response before the generator starts yielding data.

The examples use a dependency with a `Response` parameter to set the header before FastAPI creates the streaming response. Dependencies are resolved before the response is prepared, so the header is available at the correct point.

Changes:

- Add a JSON Lines tutorial section and runnable docs example for custom stream headers.
- Add an SSE tutorial section and runnable docs example for custom stream headers.
- Add tutorial tests that verify the custom header is present, the response media type is still correct, the stream body is produced, and OpenAPI keeps the expected streaming schema.

title: ⚡️ Avoid importing pydantic.v1 in Pydantic v2-only apps
body:
Follow-up to discussion #16355.

## Problem

Registering the first route imports the whole `pydantic.v1` package, even in an app that only uses Pydantic v2:

```
app.py                         @app.get("/items")
  fastapi/routing.py             add_api_route -> get_dependant -> analyze_param
    fastapi/utils.py               annotation_is_pydantic_v1(type_)
      fastapi/_compat/shared.py      from pydantic import v1
```

Since #14609 dropped `pydantic.v1` support, both callers of this detection (`fastapi/utils.py` and `fastapi/encoders.py`) exist only to raise `PydanticV1NotSupportedError`. For a v2-only app the answer is always `False`, and the import is never used for anything else. The `encoders.py` call site can also hit it during request serialization for any object that falls through `ENCODERS_BY_TYPE`.

Cost measured on FastAPI 0.141.1 / Pydantic 2.13.5 / CPython 3.14:

| | |
|---|---|
| AWS Lambda, arm64, 512 MB, cold start | **44 ms** median of 5 |
| Local, warm bytecode, `fastapi` and `pydantic` already imported | 4.2 ms median of 5 |
| On disk | 1.2 MB |

## Change

A `pydantic.v1` model class cannot exist unless `pydantic.v1` has already been imported, so `"pydantic.v1" in sys.modules` is a necessary condition for either detection function to ever return `True`. Both `is_pydantic_v1_model_class` and `is_pydantic_v1_model_instance` now return `False` early when that key is absent, before touching the import.

Behavior is unchanged for anyone who does define a v1 model: they imported `pydantic.v1` to do so, so they still get `PydanticV1NotSupportedError` with the same message. The only way to bypass the check is deleting `sys.modules["pydantic.v1"]` after defining a model, which is not a supported pattern.

## Tests

Two tests added to `tests/test_compat.py`, both using `monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, "pydantic.v1", raising=False)` so they are independent of test order:

- unit: both detection functions return `False` for a v2 model and `pydantic.v1` stays out of `sys.modules`
- integration: an app with a v2 body model handles a request end to end without importing `pydantic.v1`

The existing `tests/test_pydantic_v1_error.py` still passes, covering the branch after the guard.

title: Unwrap Annotated layers in get_stream_item_type for streaming return annotations
body:
### Discussion

- Proposed and confirmed in Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16379

---

### Description

In `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`, `get_stream_item_type(annotation)` checks if the annotation is a subclass or instance of `AsyncIterator` or `AsyncGenerator`.

However, when a route endpoint uses `Annotated[...]` in its return type annotation (e.g. `Annotated[AsyncIterator[str], ...]` or `Annotated[AsyncGenerator[str, None], ...]`), `get_stream_item_type` failed to inspect the inner stream type because `get_origin(annotation)` returns `Annotated` rather than unwrapping to the inner origin type. As a result, FastAPI fell back to non-streaming response handling.

This PR unwraps any outer/nested `Annotated` type layers using `get_args(annotation)[0]` before checking `issubclass(origin, (AsyncIterator, AsyncGenerator))`.

title: 🐛 Fix explicit response_model ignored on streaming generator endpoints
body:
## Pull Request

<!--
Please start with a GitHub Discussion.

Once a team member asks you to open a PR, create it and link the discussion here.

Typos, grammar issues, broken links and other small docs improvements should be reported in the pinned Discussion thread "✏️ Report small docs improvements, including typos or broken links".
Please do not open a PR for these yourself.
-->

Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16382

## Description

When specifying an explicit `response_model` (such as `response_model=Item`, `response_model=Iterator[Item]`, or `response_model=AsyncIterable[Item]`) on generator streaming endpoints (JSONL and SSE), it was ignored during response serialization and generated an empty OpenAPI `itemSchema: {}`.

### Root Cause
In `_populate_api_route_state()`, `get_stream_item_type()` was only called when `response_model` was an instance of `DefaultPlaceholder`. When an explicit `response_model` was provided:
1. `route.stream_item_type` was never populated, leaving `stream_item_field` as `None`.
2. `route.response_field` was erroneously populated instead.
3. At runtime, streaming endpoints serialize items via `stream_item_field`. Because it was `None`, serialization fell back to `jsonable_encoder()`, bypassing model validation and field filters (`response_model_include`, `response_model_exclude`, `response_model_exclude_none`).
4. OpenAPI generation emitted an empty `itemSchema: {}` because `stream_item_field` was absent.

### Fix
In `_populate_api_route_state()`:
- Check if the route is a streaming generator (`is_sse_stream` or `is_json_stream`) with an explicit `response_model`.
- Extract the item model using `get_stream_item_type(response_model) or response_model`.
- If it is not `ServerSentEvent`, assign `route.stream_item_type = stream_item`.
- Set `response_model = None` so `stream_item_field` is created for per-item serialization, validation, and OpenAPI generation.

### Tests Added
Added `tests/test_stream_response_model.py` covering:
- Async JSONL stream with explicit model and field filtering (`response_model_exclude`, `response_model_exclude_none`)
- Async JSONL stream with `response_model=AsyncIterable[Item]`
- Sync generator JSONL stream with `response_model=Iterator[Item]`
- SSE stream with explicit model and field exclusion
- SSE stream yielding `ServerSentEvent` directly
- SSE stream with explicit `response_model=ServerSentEvent`
- Non-streaming endpoints unaffected
- Validation error raised on invalid yielded chunk in async stream
- Validation error raised on invalid yielded chunk in sync stream
- Router inclusion via `app.include_router()`
- OpenAPI schema generation (`itemSchema` for JSONL and `contentSchema` for SSE)

title: 📝 Clarify comment about SSE event terminator
body:
Closes: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16265

## Description

The docstring of `format_sse_event` mistakenly states that each event end up with two end-of-line characters: 
https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/50113da16fec53b66b80d75e80a89296de4fa5a5/fastapi/sse.py#L210

In fact, according to the [specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream), event can be empty (no comments and no fields) and then it will be just one empty line.
So, two end-of-line characters in the end is only true for non-empty events. First end-of-line character is actually a part of field or comment and second (empty line) is an event terminator.

## AI Disclaimer

I used AI (Codex) to investigate, but it was mostly misleading until I learned how to read the notation in the spec and figured out the solution by myself and explained my thoughts. Then Codex approved my approach.
